rationale: There is clear initial clinical evidence that episodic hyperventilation is a characteristic manifestation of dominant de novo RNU2-2-associated DEE (occurring in 3/5 [60%] of patients in Chiu et al. and noted by Krygier et al., OMIM, and PanelApp). However, the specific comparative cutoffs posited in the hypothesis (>50% dominant, <10% recessive biallelic RNU2-2, and <2% RNU4-2) cannot be definitively validated as a universal discriminator across broader cohorts: Leitão et al. evaluated 35 dominant and 91 biallelic individuals and emphasized broad phenotypic overlap between dominant and recessive forms along a gradient-of-impact model, rather than a clear-cut syndromic dichotomy based on respiratory phenotypes. Furthermore, explicit quantitative documentation measuring episodic hyperventilation incidence specifically in RNU4-2 cohorts is absent in the available literature.

evidence.text: In a cohort describing the initial series of dominant RNU2-2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 3 of 5 individuals (60%) presented with episodic hyperventilation alongside obstructive sleep apnea and status epilepticus.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3).

evidence.text: A systematic analysis of 141 individuals with RNU2-2 variants (35 dominant, 91 biallelic across 73 families) showed overlapping clinical features between dominant and recessive RNU2-2 neurodevelopmental disorders, supporting a continuous gradient-of-impact model rather than a completely segregated phenotypic profile.

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
source.quote: Dominant and recessive RNU2-2 NDDs share overlapping clinical features, with frequent epilepsy. Blood transcriptomics and DNA methylation analyses revealed subtle, variant-specific effects on splicing and episignatures. Our results support a gradient-of-impact model bridging dominant and recessive inheritance

evidence.text: Biallelic RNU2-2 variants cause a distinct, highly prevalent recessive neurodevelopmental syndrome presenting as severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, with loss of expression of U2-2, yet comprehensive systematic respiratory phenotyping comparing its hyperventilation rate to dominant RNU2-2 or RNU4-2 is not formally quantified in the text.

source.title: Biallelic variants in RNU2-2 cause a remarkably frequent developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: We show that the recessive RNU2-2 syndrome is genetically, clinically and mechanistically distinct from the dominant RNU2-2 disorder. Within our cohort, the recessive RNU2-2 syndrome emerges as by far the most frequent recessive NDD

conflicts: Small initial cohorts (Chiu et al., Krygier et al.) report hyperventilation in a majority (3/5) of dominant de novo RNU2-2 patients, leading to diagnostic classification entries denoting seizures and hyperventilation; however, larger cohorts (Leitão et al.) observe substantial clinical overlap across 35 dominant and 91 recessive individuals along an allelic gradient.
Quantitative claims of hyperventilation prevalence below 10% in recessive RNU2-2 and below 2% in RNU4-2 lack direct cohort-wide comparative frequency data across standardized diagnostic registries.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic HPO-coded prevalence of episodic hyperventilation (HP:0002883) across the complete international cohort of 35 dominant versus 91 biallelic RNU2-2 patients described by Leitão et al.?
new_directions.rationale: Resolving this question with exact numerators and denominators will determine whether episodic hyperventilation maintains statistical power as an independent clinical discriminator between dominant and recessive forms.

new_directions.question_text: Does episodic hyperventilation in RNU2-2 DEE represent central autonomic dysregulation or an ictal/peri-ictal epileptic phenomenon (e.g., autonomic seizure component or post-ictal hyperpnea)?
new_directions.rationale: Krygier et al. noted hyperventilation episodes immediately preceding generalized tonic-clonic seizures, whereas Chiu et al. and OMIM report it alongside obstructive sleep apnea. Video-EEG polysomnography correlation is required to establish its pathophysiological basis.
